document_title: Named in Writing, Answered in Writing
post_copy:
"We're going to file to intervene and oppose it, just so we have a position," AEA's chief said of the proposed Cook Inlet AI data center.

Curtis W. Thayer said it to a reporter on September 14th. On October 7th, with 26 days left to file, the Alaska Energy Authority signed a motion that takes no position.

DeepGreen's application named AEA's CIPLink its "Strategic Partner." AEA told FERC it has had "no communications or relationship with DeepGreen."

By October 22nd the docket held 134 filings. None came from CIRI or the Kenaitze Indian Tribe, named in the application as coordinating.

ORPC and AEA answer the lines that named them. The chief's words face AEA's motion, and the docket's 134 filings and six would-be parties follow.

Comments and motions close at 5 p.m. Eastern on November 2nd. What will AEA's filed position say by then?

#CookInlet #FERC #SubseaDataCenters

A 48-month permit to study 100 MW from 330 to 350 tidal turbines feeding 66 hives of AI compute, on about 1,400 to 1,650 acres.

A preliminary permit gives priority to file for a license. It authorizes no construction.

aftercare: Post in a Tuesday to Thursday slot, 8 to 11 a.m. Alaska time. Tuesday, October 27th still leaves six days before the November 2nd deadline, and the cadence is the owner's call.
Paste the sources comment within 60 seconds of posting, and confirm every raw URL survives as plain text.
Check that the PDF document title reads "Named in Writing, Answered in Writing" before publishing.
Reply to every comment in the first 90 minutes. If AEA, ORPC, CIRI or the Kenaitze Indian Tribe weigh in, answer with the filing's own words and its accession number.
After 48 hours, note saves, comments and reposts for the ledger.
editor_notes_for_email: The deck puts AEA's words beside AEA's filing and lets each party speak exactly as it filed. Curtis W. Thayer's "oppose" is a quote the Peninsula Clarion published September 14th. It was never a filing, and AEA's motion keeps the right to change its no-position stance. The motion is dated October 7th and was filed October 8th. Slides 02 and 04 and the caption use the signing date and slide 08 uses the filed date, each labelled as such. ORPC's "configured to interface with" is ORPC quoting a DeepGreen filing. That sentence isn't in the February 11th application and probably sits in the June 26th supplement, which wasn't read. The CIRI and Kenaitze line means no filing was listed when the docket was pulled late on October 22nd, Alaska time. It says nothing about their views or about any contact with DeepGreen. The 117 public comment filings come from 115 distinct names, and October 13th's 18 are a weekend and holiday backlog, not a one-day surge. DeepGreen's answer also says it never claimed a formal binding partnership with AEA, and the deck doesn't show that line.
